sahil: heads-up — onboarding run for ceres-7b-q4f showed a ~3% exact-match regression vs our baseline on squad-like evals. CI flagged the eval job (attached logs).

anya: can you paste the exact eval command + model config you used? seed, quant args, and chat template pls.

sahil: sure — repro command:
```
./eval-runner --model ./models/ceres-7b-q4f --config configs/ceres_onboard.json --dataset squad_small --seed 42 --quant q4f --batch-size 8
```
config snippet:
```
{
  "model_name": "ceres-7b-q4f",
  "tokenizer": {"type": "byte_bpe", "vocab": "gpt2"},
  "chat_template": "<INST>{{prompt}}</INST>{{response}}",
  "preserve_special_tokens": false
}
```

eval-runner-bot: CI failure summary: eval-job-1798723456 exited 1. Exception: TokenizerError: special token <INST> split across tokens, merge failed. Trace: tokenizer.merge_tokens at tokenizer.py:412

mike: that alone can cause metric drift — if the sentinel gets split, prompt framing changes and generation behavior can move. Mistral/gpt-style sentinels often need explicit preservation in BPE tokenizers.

anya: does q4f quantization amplify this? iirc rounding differences + different kv-cache offsets can cause small behavior changes but not usually 3% EM.

sahil: agree, but observed two compounding issues: (1) tokenizer splitting sentinels, (2) padding mismatch in runner when batching across quantized kernels (pad id vs pad token usage). both can affect internal state.

mike: proposed quick fix to model config: set "preserve_special_tokens": true and ensure tokenizer.pad_id is used when building batches. e.g.
```
{
  "tokenizer": {"type": "byte_bpe", "vocab": "gpt2", "preserve_special_tokens": true, "pad_id": 0}
}
```

eva: i'll own a small patch: (1) make eval-runner fetch pad_id from tokenizer object instead of hardcoded 0, (2) add a canonicalizer step that prevents sentinel splits by mapping multi-token sentinels -> single token when available. i'll also add a unit test in harness/tests/test_tokenizer_preserve.py with a tiny chat template fixture.

rekha: note — for quantized runs the padding value interacts with fused-kernel dispatch (we had a bug earlier where pad=-1 used in cpu path but 0 assumed in GPU kernels). test needs to cover CPU/GPU paths.

sahil: +1. eva, can you also add a canary eval that runs the exact protege prompt that triggered the regression? small dataset, run under CI nightly for new model onboarding.

eva: yes — opening PR now. PR will include:
- runner: use tokenizer.pad_id
- tokenizer: option preserve_special_tokens default true for new model configs
- tests: tokenizer preserve + batch padding across CPU/GPU
- small canary dataset and a short cron job in CI

mike: small patch suggestion for runner (Python):
```
pad_id = tokenizer.pad_id if hasattr(tokenizer, 'pad_id') else config.get('pad_id', 0)
batch = pad_sequences(seqs, pad_value=pad_id)
```

sahil: that looks right. also add a deterministic seed path for quantized inference: --stable-quant true to disable non-deterministic rounding in the quant backend.

quant-bot: quant-profile note: enabling stable rounding toggles per-op deterministic kernels. CLI flag: `--stable-quant=true`. recommend running before claiming regression is fixed.

anya: can we add an eval-harness gating rule: if new model onboarding changes EM by >1.5% vs verified baseline, require manual review (ticket) before merge?

eva: yes — i'll add a step in the onboarding workflow: post eval summary to #eng-ml with metrics and diff, and block auto-merge if abs(delta) > 1.5% EM or >2% ROUGE.

sahil: perfect. thanks all — assigning follow-ups: @eva will open PR and tests, @mike will review padding changes, @anya will rerun quant experiments with `--stable-quant=true` once PR lands.

mike: lgtm

anya: thx :heart: 

eval-runner-bot: CI link: https://ci.redwood/1798723456 (will update when PR created)

sahil: i'll re-run the original job once the patch lands and report back here.
